---
title: "Broader Community"
---

BRUG exists within a rich landscape of data science and research communities at UW–Madison. Whether you are looking for statistical consulting, library support, a student club, or a community of practice focused on machine learning, the groups below are worth knowing about. We think of them as neighbors — different doors into the same larger project of open, rigorous, reproducible research.

---

## Campus Services

**[The Data Science Hub](https://hub.datascience.wisc.edu/)**
The Data Science Hub in the Data Science Institute provides data science training and implements data science into research practices across campus. The Data Science Hub executes a mission for community engagement and learning opportunities for campus researchers through a variety of services, including:

**[SSCC — Social Science Computing Cooperative](https://www.sscc.wisc.edu)**
Statistical computing support, consulting, and training for UW–Madison 
researchers. A long-standing resource with deep expertise in R, Stata, and 
related tools.

**[Library Research Guides — R Programming Workshops](https://researchguides.library.wisc.edu/R/why)**
UW–Madison Libraries and Ebling Library offer R programming workshops for graduate students, faculty, staff, and undergraduates working with tabular research data. Content draws from the Data Carpentry R Ecology lessons.

**[Research Data Services](https://researchdata.wisc.edu)**
A free campus resource offering consultations, training, and guidance on research data management and sharing — including data citation, open access, repository selection, and compliance with funder and publisher policies.

---

## Student Clubs

**[The Badger BioData Initiative](https://badgerbiodata.github.io/the-ecosystem/)**
An undergraduate club focused on biological data projects and modern research methods. They create a space on campus to learn and explore working with biological data at your own pace. If you are an undergraduate interested in learning bioinformatics or biocomputation, this is the perfect place to start. 

---

## Communities of Practice

**[ML+X](https://mlplus.wisconsin.edu)**
ML+X is a community of practice at UW–Madison that connects students, researchers, and professionals who apply machine learning (ML) methods across various domains. Hosted by the Data Science Institute, the community is designed for researchers tackling specific applications—the "X"—ranging from the social sciences to ecology and medicine

**[UW Research Software Engineering Community](https://hub.datascience.wisc.edu/communities/research-software-engineering-community/)**
The UW Research Software Engineering Community (UW RSE) is a place to learn and share ideas, methods, and best practices on data engineering and software engineering components of research across domains. The UW RSE community is open to anyone affiliated with UW-Madison who is engaged in, or interested in, research software engineering. Madison community members are also welcome to join sessions of interest.

**[Badger Data Network](https://data.wisc.edu/badgeranalyticsusergroup/)**

The Badger Data Network is a vibrant community uniting data, analytics, visualization, and business intelligence enthusiasts, promotes using institutional data to support progress and implement strategic initiatives. 

**[UW Data Wonks](https://datawonks.wisc.edu/)**

Data Wonks is a Community of Practice (CoP) for members of the UW-Madison community who are interested in data and related technology. Through a variety of events, networking, and materials on this website we hope to help people access, process, interpret, and present data using a variety of tools and methods.
